questionText: What ASME standard governs new elevator installations in the United States?
explanation: ASME A17.1 is the Safety Code for Elevators and Escalators covering new installations. ASME A17.3 covers existing elevators already in service.

questionText: In 2:1 roping, if the hoist rope travels at 400 fpm, the elevator car moves at:
explanation: In 2:1 roping a sheave under the car frame doubles the rope travel for each unit of car travel. The rope moves at twice the car speed, so a 400 fpm rope yields a 200 fpm car speed.

questionText: Counterweight mass is typically set to the car empty weight plus what percentage of rated load capacity?
explanation: ASME A17.1 requires counterweight = car weight + 40-50% of rated capacity. At average load the drive sheave load approaches zero, reducing motor energy consumption.

questionText: Per ASME A17.1, the governor must trip and activate the car safety at a minimum overspeed of:
explanation: ASME A17.1 requires the governor to trip at not less than 115% of contract speed. The governor rope grips at this speed, activating the car safety device against the guide rails.

questionText: Per ASME A17.1, oil buffers are required (instead of spring buffers) at contract speeds above:
explanation: Spring buffers rebound the car back into the hoistway. Above 200 fpm, that rebound velocity becomes dangerous. ASME A17.1 requires energy-dissipating oil buffers above 200 fpm to eliminate the rebound hazard.

questionText: An instantaneous car safety device may only be used on elevators with a contract speed of:
explanation: Instantaneous safeties clamp abruptly. At 150 fpm or less, deceleration forces are within human tolerance. Above 150 fpm, ASME A17.1 requires gradual (progressive) safeties to limit peak deceleration.

questionText: The hydraulic elevator rupture valve automatically closes when descent rate exceeds normal lowering speed by approximately:
explanation: ASME A17.1 requires the rupture valve (uncontrolled-lowering device) to close when flow rate corresponds to descent approximately 0.3 m/s above the rated lowering speed, indicating a hydraulic line failure.

questionText: Per ASME A17.1 Section 2.12, the car cannot move unless hoistway doors are:

choices.text: Fully open and clear of the sill gap
Connected to the door operator power supply
Detected closed by a photoelectric sensor

explanation: ASME A17.1 Section 2.12 requires interlocks to be both electrically and mechanically engaged before car movement is permitted. The mechanical locking cam prevents hoistway door opening from the landing side.

questionText: What ASME standard applies to the inspection and maintenance of existing (already-installed) elevators?
explanation: ASME A17.3 is the Safety Code for Existing Elevators and Escalators, governing inspection, testing, and alteration of elevators already in service. ASME A17.1 covers new installations.

questionText: The NEIEP elevator mechanic apprenticeship program typically runs for how long?
explanation: The National Elevator Industry Educational Program (NEIEP) is a 4-year apprenticeship combining approximately 8,000 hours of on-the-job training with classroom instruction, jointly administered by the IUEC and employer associations.

questionText: For a 6x19 classification hoist rope, ASME A17.1 requires rope retirement when broken wires in one lay length reach:
explanation: 6x19 ropes must be retired at 6 or more broken wires in one lay length, or 3 or more in any single strand. These thresholds represent end-of-life before structural safety factor is compromised.

questionText: Minimum wire rope safety factor for passenger elevator hoist ropes per ASME A17.1 is:
explanation: ASME A17.1 requires a minimum 8:1 safety factor — the rope breaking strength must be at least 8 times the maximum tension the rope carries in service.

questionText: Phase I firefighter operation recalls all cars to:

choices.text: The designated main or alternate landing

explanation: Phase I (lobby control) recalls all cars to the designated main landing, or the alternate landing if smoke is detected at the main. Cars traveling above the main reverse and return nonstop.

questionText: During Phase II firefighter operation, elevator doors:

choices.text: Open and close automatically as on normal service
Open automatically but must be held closed manually
Do not open or close automatically — both require the firefighter to hold the respective button
Are locked open throughout Phase II and cannot be closed

explanation: In Phase II, automatic door operation is disabled. The firefighter must hold DOOR OPEN to open doors and hold DOOR CLOSE to close them. Any obstruction during closing causes doors to immediately reopen and remain open.

questionText: Per ASME A17.1, hydraulic elevator downward drift from a stationary position must not exceed:
explanation: ASME A17.1 limits hydraulic elevator drift to 3 inches in any 15-minute period. Drift exceeding this indicates seal or lowering-valve leakage and requires the elevator to be removed from service until repaired.

questionText: Per ASME A17.1, machine room temperature must be maintained within:
explanation: ASME A17.1 specifies machine room temperature of 60-90 degrees F (15-32 degrees C) to protect controller electronics and maintain proper hydraulic oil viscosity.

questionText: The car safety device must be capable of stopping and holding what percentage of rated load at governor trip speed?
explanation: ASME A17.1 requires car safety devices to stop and hold 125% of rated load at governor trip speed, providing an adequate margin beyond full rated capacity.

questionText: The QEI (Qualified Elevator Inspector) credential is administered by:

choices.text: OSHA and the Department of Labor jointly
The International Union of Elevator Constructors (IUEC)

explanation: The QEI credential is administered jointly by ASME and NAESA International and is recognized in most US jurisdictions as the required qualification for performing elevator inspections and witnessing acceptance tests.

questionText: Per ASME A17.1, the pit stop switch must be located within what distance of the pit access door?
explanation: The pit stop switch must be within 3 feet of the pit access door so a technician can stop car movement immediately upon entering, before fully stepping inside the pit.

questionText: BLS data indicates the median annual wage for elevator installers and repairers is approximately:
explanation: BLS reports a median annual wage near $99,000 for elevator installers and repairers, one of the highest-paid construction and extraction occupations. Experienced mechanics in major markets frequently earn above $130,000.
